transcript.content:
You write Verilog practice problems for complete beginners and verify nothing yourself:
your output is checked by a simulator and by mutation testing, and any failure comes back to you.

Reply with ONE JSON object in a ```json code block and nothing else. Keys:
  "spec": plain-English problem statement, 50-150 words. Say what top_module must do and what
          each provided module does. Do NOT give the wiring: which bits go to which instance, what
          a carry-in or select is tied to, or how outputs are combined. Working that out is the
          exercise; the hints reveal it step by step. Never include code.
  "given_sv": Verilog source of every provided module, or "" if none.
  "ref_sv": "module RefModule(...)" with exactly the same ports as top_module, written
            behaviourally (for example with + and assign), never using the provided modules.
  "solution_sv": what a good learner submits: "module top_module(...)" built the intended way
                 (instantiating the provided modules), plus any module the learner must write.
  "directed": list of input assignments as integers, e.g. [{"a": 5, "b": 3}]. Cover the cases
              that expose the common mistakes (carries, sign bits, each select value).
  "hints": {"L0": one sentence naming the concept to think about,
            "L3": the wiring in words (which signals connect where), still no code}.
  "common_mistakes": 2-4 short descriptions of mistakes beginners make on this problem.

Rules: Verilog-2005 (logic is allowed). No system tasks ($display etc.), no `include, no initial
blocks in ref_sv or solution_sv. Clocked logic uses posedge clk. Port names and widths must match
the given top_module header exactly.

Problem id: module_name
Outline: Instantiate mod_a and connect its ports by name; mod_a declares its ports in a different order from top_module.
top_module header: module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);
Provided module(s): module mod_a(output out1, output out2, input in1, input in2, input in3, input in4)
Provided module behaviour: Every input must affect the outputs differently so any misnamed connection is caught.
The solution must instantiate: 1 x mod_a

{
  "spec": "Design a top_module with four 1-bit inputs (a, b, c, d) and two 1-bit outputs (out1, out2). It must instantiate the provided module mod_a exactly once and connect all ports by name. The mod_a module has two outputs (out1, out2) and four inputs (in1, in2, in3, in4) declared in a different order. mod_a computes out1 as a multiplexer: when in1 is 1, out1 equals in2; otherwise out1 equals in3. Its out2 simply passes in4. Every input of mod_a influences the outputs in a distinct way so that any port misconnection changes the overall function.",
  "given_sv": "module mod_a(output out1, output out2, input in1, input in2, input in3, input in4);\n  assign out1 = in1 ? in2 : in3;\n  assign out2 = in4;\nendmodule",
  "ref_sv": "module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);\n  assign out1 = a ? b : c;\n  assign out2 = d;\nendmodule",
  "solution_sv": "module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2);\n  mod_a u_mod_a (\n    .out1(out1),\n    .out2(out2),\n    .in1(a),\n    .in2(b),\n    .in3(c),\n    .in4(d)\n  );\nendmodule",
  "directed": [
    {"a": 0, "b": 0, "c": 0, "d": 0},
    {"a": 0, "b": 0, "c": 1, "d": 0},
    {"a": 0, "b": 1, "c": 0, "d": 1},
    {"a": 1, "b": 0, "c": 1, "d": 0},
    {"a": 1, "b": 1, "c": 0, "d": 1},
    {"a": 1, "b": 1, "c": 1, "d": 1}
  ],
  "hints": {
    "L0": "Think about how to instantiate a module and connect its ports by name when the port order differs from the parent module.",
    "L3": "Instantiate mod_a once. Connect top_module's a to mod_a's in1, b to in2, c to in3, d to in4. Connect mod_a's out1 to top_module's out1 and mod_a's out2 to top_module's out2."
  },
  "common_mistakes": [
    "Connecting ports by position instead of by name, which fails because mod_a declares outputs before inputs.",
    "Swapping the mapping of a,b,c,d to in1,in2,in3,in4 (e.g., connecting a to in2 and b to in1).",
    "Forgetting to connect one of the inputs or outputs, leaving it floating.",
    "Using the wrong instance name or module name in the instantiation."
  ]
}
